Patch Set 11:

(2 comments)
From security side, should we list bootstrap account as part of bmcweb, ipmi etc ?

It is depend on the sign in accounts and interfaces:

1. For bmcweb, if the account with administrator roles. The bootStrap account will be showed and can be managed by admin accounts.
For the other type of user roles, the bootStrap account will not be showed.

2. For the ipmi, the bootStrap account will not be showed because the bootStrap accounts are not belong to ipmi groups.
I don't think that we should hard code the Host0 object path.

Currently, the `xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host` D-Bus interface will be hosted by `xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host` service. Although there can be more than one /xyz/openbmc_project/state/host* object paths handle `xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host` D-Bus interface. The first host `host0` should be existed.
So using "/xyz/openbmc_project/state/host0" to check the currentHostState is reasonable ATM.

Not clear why this is required. Can you please help explain need of this function ?

I think you need review the patch set carefully to understand about the need of the function. The `Brief` already details the purpose of function `remove argument from the configuration/storage file`.

For short, to support removing the bootStrap Account in reset of the phosphor-user-manager services, we need to store the BootStrapAccount user to one configuration file name `/etc/bootStrap.conf`. When the service restarts, it will recovery the list of user accounts. but for the bootStrap accounts they should be removed. `removeConfKey` function is added to allow remove on bootStrapAccount configuration in `/etc/bootStrap.conf`

The purpose is adding or updating "<username>=1" line to the `/etc/bootStrap.conf` configuration file.
